name: Borynia Palace

highlights: A Classicist palace on a rectangular plan with late-Baroque influences, a compact form and a mansard roof, with Corinthian pilasters and projecting bays on its façades
Built in the second half of the 18th century, when the surrounding land belonged to Jan (Johann) von Schlutterbach, an Austrian nobleman
Borynia was a knightly village held by a succession of noble families, including the von Madeyski, von Raczek and Ledóchowski families
A local legend tells of a White Lady, said to be the first owner's granddaughter
It stands in a park with a 600-year-old oak
Today it is a hotel with a restaurant open to the public and conference rooms
description:
The palace in Borynia, now part of Jastrzębie-Zdrój, was built in the second half of the 18th century, when the surrounding land belonged to Jan von Schlutterbach, an Austrian nobleman. It is a Classicist building on a rectangular plan with late-Baroque influences, a compact mass and a mansard roof, its façades decorated with Corinthian pilasters and projecting bays.

Borynia was a knightly village that passed through several noble families, among them the von Madeyski, von Raczek and Ledóchowski families. A local legend of a White Lady is probably linked to the first owner's granddaughter.

The palace stands in a park with a 600-year-old oak and now houses a three-star hotel with a restaurant open to the public and conference rooms.
